premises.statement: Selecting the highest version and then the greatest updated_timestamp for each email_template_id is an acceptable replacement for filtering metadata by is_most_recent_version.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email_template_id ORDER BY version DESC, updated_timestamp DESC) AS version_rank ... WHERE t.version_rank = 1
premises.alternative: The contract says to "keep only rows marked as the most recent version"; the new code ignores that flag and emits "TRUE AS is_most_recent_version".
premises.reason: The replacement can select different template metadata or include templates with no marked current version.

premises.statement: Rows tied for the highest version and updated_timestamp within an email_template_id have identical output metadata.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email_template_id ORDER BY version DESC, updated_timestamp DESC)
premises.reason: Conflicting tied rows would make the selected template metadata arbitrary.

premises.statement: Every non-null program start_date and end_date has its intended calendar date represented by its first ten characters in a format DuckDB can cast to DATE.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: TRY_CAST(SUBSTR(start_date, 1, 10) AS DATE) and TRY_CAST(SUBSTR(end_date, 1, 10) AS DATE)
premises.reason: Other date representations would silently become null or yield a different date after truncation.
